en.title: Houses with Different Colors for Neighbors and Mirror Pairs
en.description:
An even number n of houses stand in a row and are painted with three fixed colors. Any two adjacent houses, and any two houses at the same distance from the two ends, must have different colors. The original snapshot clearly says different colors; the same color in the catalog is an error. Output the answer modulo 10⁹+7. This catalog entry shares its source with an earlier problem; it keeps its own problem ID and is verified independently.

The input/output protocol and the explicitly marked supplementary constraints were compiled by this site; upstream solutions are not executed.
en.input: One line with an even n in 2..100000.
en.output: Output the single integer required by the problem.
en.explanation: The answers to the three public examples are, in order: 6; 18; 54. The examples were rechecked by independent enumeration, state search, or direct simulation.
hints: Paint pair by pair from both ends toward the middle: the first pair has 6 options, and every later pair has 3.
